transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time someone else needs more, but... well, I'm just here because I feel a bit worn down, I guess? Almost all the time, really. Even after a full night's sleep, which I know sounds silly, but I just wake up tired. And by the time I've handled my work at the lab and tried to tackle the clutter around the house, I just... I have very little energy left for anything else. Is that... does that make sense to come in for?
Do you often feel sad?

Um... I don't know if I'd use the word sad, exactly. I definitely don't want to sound ungrateful for what I have, or like I'm just complaining. It's more like... most days, there's just this low, gray mood sort of running in the background? 

I mean, I still go to the lab and talk to people just fine, I promise I'm keeping up with my responsibilities. But I just... I don't really feel light or excited about things anymore. Even my hobbies, like baking, or taking out my telescope the way I used to. I just sort of go through the motions. I hope I'm explaining that right... does that sound like what you mean by sad?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Oh, um... well, it's been a little while. I really hope you're not frustrated that I waited so long to come in. I just kept thinking I could snap myself out of it if I just tried harder, you know? 

But I think this... this sort of low baseline has been going on for a little over two years now. It started shortly after we moved into our current place—it's an older house, so there was a lot to do, and I just figured I was naturally tired from the move and getting everything set up. But the feeling just kind of stayed, even after we settled in. 

Is... is two years a really bad amount of time to let something like this go? I really hope I haven't made things worse by waiting, I just didn't want to make a fuss over nothing.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Well... I mean, I still *like* them. I really do! I don't want you to think I just sit around moping all weekend. When I do get the telescope set up, it's... it's nice. I think maybe I'm just a bit too worn out from the lab to fully appreciate it right now? 

So it's not that I don't enjoy things at all, it just... takes a lot more effort to get started, and the spark isn't quite as bright as it used to be. I still think baking is a good time, I just haven't noticed myself actually wanting to do it lately. I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or unmotivated... I really am trying to keep up with my normal routines. Did I answer that okay?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Um... I guess that's sort of similar to what I was just saying? I really wouldn't use the words 'lost interest,' exactly. That sounds so... final, you know? Like I've just given up on my life, and I promise I haven't done that. 

I still care about my hobbies. I still read the astronomy journals when they come into the lab, and I still like the *idea* of trying out a new recipe. It's just... maybe the follow-through isn't quite there right now? So, no, I don't think I've completely lost interest in them. I just haven't had the energy to actually do them as much. 

I hope I'm understanding your question right, and not just repeating myself... is that what you were asking?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past two years?

Oh, um... no, not really. My clothes all still fit pretty much the exact same as they did before we moved. 

I always try to make sure I'm eating properly and taking care of myself, even on the days I'm feeling a bit more run down from the lab. So my weight has been really steady. I... I hope that's a good sign? Like, at least I'm keeping up with my physical health, right? I'd really hate for you to think I was just letting myself go.
Have you ever had thoughts about death or dying?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know things have been a bit harder lately, but I would never... I don't think like that. 

I really value my life, and I have my job at the lab, and... I just want to get back to feeling like myself again, you know? I'm just feeling a little tired, that's all. I really hope you don't think I'm in some kind of crisis, because I promise I'm not. I'm just trying to figure out why I've been in this slump. That's a normal thing to want to figure out, right?
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Guilty? Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, everyone feels a little bad when they make a mistake at work or, you know, forget to call a friend back, but... I don't walk around feeling guilty all the time. 

I try really hard to do the right thing and be responsible, especially at the lab. I'm always very careful to pull my weight so I don't let anyone down. So there's really no reason for me to feel guilty, right? I... I hope it doesn't sound like I'm doing something I shouldn't be. I really do try my best to be a good person.
Do you feel like you no longer get pleasure from things that used to make you happy?

Oh, um... no, I still enjoy things. I mean, I still love reading or, you know, just relaxing with a good show after work. And I still get a lot of satisfaction out of my projects at the lab. 

I'm definitely not just sitting around miserable all day. I... I still find plenty of things to smile about. That's a really positive sign, isn't it? I always try to keep a good attitude and focus on the things I like doing, so... I hope you can see I'm really trying to stay upbeat. I wouldn't want you to think I've just given up on enjoying life.
Do you feel like it takes more effort than it used to for you to feel happy or excited about things?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But it's not like I'm completely unable to feel happy. I mean, I still go into the lab every day and chat with my coworkers, and I'm perfectly fine. 

It's just... I suppose most days there's this sort of low, gray feeling running in the background. Like, I used to get really excited about baking on the weekends, or taking out my telescope when the sky was clear, and lately... I just don't feel quite as light or enthusiastic about doing those things. But I'm still doing okay overall! I just have to push myself a tiny bit more, which is pretty normal when you're busy and tired, right? I'm sure everyone has phases where their hobbies feel like a little more effort. I really hope you don't think I'm just sitting around moping all the time, because I'm definitely still trying my best to stay engaged with everything.
Has your low, gray mood been constant over the past two years, or have you had periods where it lifted and then returned?

Oh, um... I'm really not sure. I haven't kept track of it that closely. Two years sounds like such a long time, and I... I definitely wouldn't want you to think I've just been walking around under a cloud for years on end. 

I mean, I have plenty of good days! And periods where everything feels completely fine. I try really hard not to dwell on the gray days, you know? I just try to keep moving forward and focus on my work and the people around me. So I haven't really noticed an exact pattern of it, like, lifting and returning. 

I hope that's a helpful answer... I just try to stay as positive as I can, so I don't really have a strict timeline for you. I hope that's okay? I really am trying my best to just handle things as they come.
Have you had any periods over the past two years where you felt completely back to your normal self?

Um... well, I guess I feel like I'm my normal self most of the time! I mean, I haven't really noticed any big, dramatic shifts where I felt completely different or anything. I'm still just me, you know? Going to the lab and doing my work and everything. 

I haven't really kept track of... like, a specific timeline of when things felt one hundred percent perfect versus just okay. It's mostly just that little bit of extra effort I mentioned before. But I definitely don't feel like I've lost myself or turned into someone else. I'm still functioning totally fine. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely broken or anything... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that helpful at all?
Do you think your low, gray mood tends to come and go in episodes, or is it more steady?

Well, um... I guess I'd say it's more steady? Like, it doesn't really hit me in big, dramatic waves or anything like that. It's just sort of... there. But it's very mild! I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. 

I mean, I still have plenty of moments where I'm laughing with my coworkers or enjoying a good cup of coffee. It's not like a constant, heavy burden that ruins my whole day. It's just a tiny bit of background noise, you know? 

I hope I'm making sense. I just want to be sure I'm explaining it right, so you don't think I'm just miserable all the time. Does that make sense? I'm really trying to give you the most accurate picture I can.
Have you ever had a period of time, say a few weeks or months, where your low mood and lack of energy were significantly worse than they are now?

Oh, gosh, no. Um... I really don't think so. I mean, I've never had a time where I couldn't get out of bed or do my work at the lab. I always make sure to keep up with my responsibilities... I wouldn't let it get that bad, you know? 

It's always just been this very manageable, mild sort of feeling. I definitely haven't had any big crashes or months where I couldn't function. I just keep plugging along. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just really wouldn't want you to think I've ever completely fallen apart or been unable to cope. I've always managed to hold everything together pretty well, I think. Does that make sense?
Has your low mood lasted for two years continuously, without any breaks?

Well, um... I suppose it has been a while. I think I first started noticing this... this sort of low baseline feeling right after we moved into our older house. And that was, gosh, a little over two years ago now. 

But I mean, I wouldn't call it a continuous, awful slump or anything! It's just been this very subtle, mild thing in the background since then. I've still been totally fine and getting everything done, I promise. It's really not a big deal at all. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline without making it sound like I've been miserable for two whole years, because I really haven't been. Is that the kind of information you needed?
Has your low mood lasted for at least two years without any periods of at least two months where you felt completely back to normal?

Um... well, like I mentioned, I first noticed this sort of low baseline feeling right after we moved into our house, which was a little over two years ago. And... I guess since then, I haven't really had a full two months where it completely went away. 

But I mean, I don't want that to sound like I've been just stuck in a rut the whole time! There are definitely days or even a couple of weeks where I feel really good and everything is totally fine. It's just that... well, the subtle background feeling always sort of creeps back in before a full two months have passed. 

I really hope I'm explaining this right... I just don't want you to think I'm broken or that I haven't had any good times at all over the last two years, because I have! I'm still doing okay, really. Does that make sense? Am I answering your question the way you need?
Has there ever been a period of at least two months in the past two years where you felt completely back to your normal self, without this low, gray mood?

Oh, um, I'm sorry, I hope I didn't confuse you just a second ago! I know I might be rambling a bit. But, um... yeah, to answer your question directly... no, I haven't. 

Like I was mentioning, this sort of low baseline has been going on since shortly after we moved into the older house, which was a little over two years ago now. And since then, I haven't really had a full, uninterrupted block of two months where it was completely gone. 

But I really am still functioning perfectly well, I promise! It's just a very mild, background thing. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact information you need since you asked again. Is that... does that help clear it up for you? I really want to be helpful.
Has your low mood been present for most of every day over the past two years?

Um... well, most days, yes. It's just... it's like this low, gray feeling running in the background for most of the day. 

But it doesn't stop me from doing what I need to do! I still go into the lab every day, and I talk to people, and I get my work done. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing, because I'm really not. It's just that... well, I don't really feel that lightness or excitement about things anymore. Like, I used to love baking, or going out to check the telescope, and now I just... I don't feel that same spark for them most days. 

But I'm still keeping up with everything, I promise. It's just a very mild thing. Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details.
Has your low mood been present for at least two years without any periods of remission?

Um, I know we've kind of gone over this a few times, and I'm really sorry if I'm not being clear enough! I definitely don't want to make your job harder. 

But yes, um, like I said, this sort of low baseline feeling started shortly after we moved into our house, which was a little over two years ago. And since then, it hasn't really gone away completely for any long stretch of time. 

But it's really not severe! It's just a very mild, quiet thing in the background. I'm still me, and I'm still handling everything just fine. I just... I hope I'm making sense and giving you the right answer this time? I'm really trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
